titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 7/2010 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިދާރީ ދާއިރާތައް ލާމަރުކަޒީ އުސޫލުން ހިންގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Decentralization Act (Law No. 7/2010). It makes the staff of the Local Government Authority, the body that oversees island and city councils, civil servants, hired and dismissed by the Civil Service Commission instead of the Authority's board. The Authority's chief executive officer would draft the staff structure, the Civil Service Commission would approve it, and the National Pay Commission would set pay. The bill also adds waste management to the list of public services in Article 69-1(a).
whyItMatters: Local Government Authority staff would move into the civil service, with pay set by the National Pay Commission. Waste management would be listed alongside the other services named in Article 69-1(a).
keyProvisions: Repeals Article 61(lh), which gave the Authority's board the power to appoint and dismiss staff.

New Article 61-3(a) and (b): the Civil Service Commission appoints and dismisses the Authority's staff on the chief executive officer's advice, and the chief executive officer takes the role of the responsible senior official under Article 63 of the Civil Service Act (5/2007) for all staff matters.

New Article 61-3(c) to (e): the chief executive officer drafts a structure of posts, grades and duties on the board's advice, the Civil Service Commission approves it, and the National Pay Commission sets salaries and allowances under the State Wage Policy Act (11/2016).
Adds waste management services as item (4) under Article 69-1(a).

Transitional deadlines: the Authority submits the staff structure within 30 days of the law taking effect, the Commission approves it within 15 days, pay is set within 30 days after that, and staff are moved into the new posts within 60 days of pay being set.
The law takes effect when published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Staff of the Local Government Authority, the Civil Service Commission and National Pay Commission, and island and city councils that provide public services.
statedReasons: The government says the bill makes Local Government Authority staff civil servants to strengthen how the Authority is run, and lets councils run waste management as one of the public services they provide.
